clue.text: Its blades trim others

parts.note: the blades sound like knives or swords, but the others trimmed are blades of grass on a lawn

explanation.surface: A riddle about something with blades that cuts other blades.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the two senses of 'blades': the cutting edges of a garden machine and the blades of grass it shortens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn machine with rotating cutters shortens the grass, whose leaves are called blades.

clue.text: Advantage of diamonds for girls as a facet of US policy?

definitions.text: Advantage of diamonds for girls as a facet of US policy?

parts.words: Advantage of diamonds for girls as a facet of US policy?
parts.note: Marilyn sang that diamonds are a girl's best friend, her creed, which shares its name with an American foreign policy

explanation.surface: A question about why girls prefer gems, dressed up as American policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Marilyn Monroe sang 'Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend' – her doctrine; the real Monroe Doctrine (1823) warned Europe off the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: President Monroe's 1823 policy opposed European colonisation in the Americas, and the name also suggests Marilyn's belief in gems.

clue.text: Stock-in-trade was seen round about

indicators.note: the word was goes round the short word for about

parts.note: taken as written
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone's merchandise was spotted nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered for sale are a trader's stock.

clue.text: Goads Christopher, the tinker, without due cause

parts.note: needles means provokes or goads
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the prologue of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A tinker called Christopher provokes people for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Sly is the tinker tricked into thinking he is a lord in The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unnecessarily means doing it with no good reason.

clue.text: One is in some trouble with one's understatement

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person admits to some difficulty, with typical understatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal: I, IS and SOME are stirred together; 'in' and 'with one's' just link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric this Greek term means litotes or deliberate understatement, as in calling a disaster 'a bit of bother'.

clue.text: A spell rent-free, perhaps? …

parts.note: a magic charm that cannot be torn, split as can't plus rip, so rent-free in the sense of untearable

explanation.surface: A period living somewhere without paying rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' here means torn, not paid for housing: a CANT RIP spell can't be ripped. A cantrip is a Scots word for a magic spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect uses this word for a witch's charm or magic incantation.

clue.text: … a desire one may have after seven years

definitions.text: a desire one may have after seven years

parts.words: a desire one may have after seven years
parts.note: refers to the seven-year urge for infidelity in marriage, from the Marilyn Monroe film

explanation.surface: A longing that sets in after seven years, continuing the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'seven-year itch' is the supposed urge to stray after seven years of marriage; the dots link it to 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless craving is an urge, as in the phrase about wandering spouses after seven years.

clue.text: Learning to include the fifteen-aside game in book form

indicators.note: the book form takes in the game's abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an edition is a form in which a book is published
RU is rugby union, played fifteen a side

explanation.surface: Studying how to put rugby into a published book.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union has fifteen players a side, abbreviated RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarly knowledge acquired through study.

clue.text: Sweet Russian girl beloved of Werther

parts.note: Charlotte is the woman young Werther loves in Goethe's novel
russe is French for Russian

explanation.surface: A Russian girl adored by Goethe's lovesick hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Goethe's The Sorrows of Young Werther the hero pines for Charlotte (Lotte).
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is a mould of sponge fingers filled with custard cream, a pudding.

clue.text: One having his capital in Czechoslovakia

definitions.text: One having his capital in Czechoslovakia

parts.words: One having his capital in Czechoslovakia
parts.note: a native of the country whose capital is Oslo, which sits inside the spelling of the word Czechoslovakia

explanation.surface: Seemingly a puzzle about someone whose capital city lies in Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: No capital of Czechoslovakia fits; instead look inside the word itself: czechOSLOvakia holds OSLO, the capital of Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Norway has Oslo as the capital of their homeland.

clue.text: Girlish passion for drink

definitions.meaning: an infatuation, like a schoolgirl's for a pop star
a fizzy fruit drink, as in orange ..., made from squeezed fruit

explanation.surface: A young girl's fondness for something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolgirl's infatuation is a classic example of this word, and a squashed-fruit soft drink carries the same name.

clue.text: Bird taken by car to show

indicators.note: the bird is joined on after the word car to make the show, so removing car from the show leaves it

parts.note: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical, a show
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is given a lift in a car to an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as: the bird, taken by CAR, becomes the show CAROUSEL; strip CAR from CAROUSEL to get the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old spelling of ouzel, a thrush-like bird such as the blackbird or ring ouzel.

clue.text: Scottish wear for a British isle

definitions.meaning: a Scots word for a shirt or chemise
one of the Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A Scottish garment worn on a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small Channel Island; the same word is Scots dialect for a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots dialect uses the word for a shirt, and it is also the name of a small Channel Island.

clue.text: One said to be prone to misrepresentation

definitions.text: One said to be prone to misrepresentation

parts.words: One said to be prone to misrepresentation
parts.note: a person who lies down sounds the same as a person who tells untruths, and such a person habitually misrepresents

explanation.surface: Someone reputed to have a tendency to distort the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' hints at lying flat: a 'lier' (one lying down) sounds like the fibber, and 'said' points to that sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths misrepresents the facts, and one who reclines is lying prone.

clue.text: NCO makes crafty raid in Lancaster, for example

indicators.note: the rearranged raid goes inside the aircraft word

parts.note: the Avro Lancaster was a WWII heavy bomber aircraft

indicators.note: crafty suggests cunning manipulation, so the letters of raid are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sergeant carries out a cunning attack in a wartime plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. The Lancaster was a famous RAF wartime bomber; a bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British artillery this rank is a non-commissioned officer, equivalent to a corporal.

clue.text: Puts down record breaking quantities of medicine

indicators.note: the record breaks into the medicine quantities, splitting the word open

parts.note: measured amounts of a drug are doses
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a record-breaking amount of medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record breaking' looks like a phrase meaning unprecedented; in fact EP (record) breaks into DOSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove or put them down from power.

clue.text: All hope I'm turning into a classical Jenny Lind

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Hope is turning a person into an old-style opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind was 'the Swedish Nightingale'; in Greek myth Philomela was changed into a nightingale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish soprano was nicknamed a nightingale, and in Greek myth Philomela became that songbird, hence a classical one.

clue.text: Stipulation is for and against one in this way

parts.note: pro means in favour of
v is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A condition that argues both for and against one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement, a stipulation.

clue.text: Mowgli's kite went ahead, suffering from cold

parts.note: Chil is the kite (bird of prey) in Kipling's Jungle Book, which features Mowgli
led means went in front

explanation.surface: In the Jungle Book a bird leads the way while the boy feels cold.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's The Jungle Book the kite (a bird of prey) is called Chil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling cold is chilled through.

clue.text: Cover-up on Lady Hamilton — a difficult choice

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cover is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid covers a pot
Emma, Lady Hamilton, was Nelson's mistress

explanation.surface: A scandalous cover-up concerning Nelson's lover poses a hard decision.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' signals reading the cover word from bottom to top. Emma Hamilton was Nelson's famous mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a predicament with two unattractive options.

clue.text: It can be shuffled from time to time

definitions.text: It can be shuffled from time to time

parts.words: It can be shuffled from time to time
parts.note: sounds like a pack of cards, but refers to a prime minister's reshuffle of senior ministers

explanation.surface: Apparently a pack of cards that gets shuffled now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffled' suggests cards; British prime ministers periodically 'reshuffle' their senior ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's senior ministers form a body whose membership a prime minister changes in a reshuffle.

clue.text: Declare wrongly exculpated

indicators.note: wrongly means not in the right order, so the letters of declare are rearranged

explanation.surface: To announce someone wrongly freed of blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exculpated has been found not guilty, absolved of blame.

clue.text: Bird moving in the rank or file

definitions.text: moving in the rank or file
definitions.meaning: the chess piece that moves along rows and columns, also called a castle

explanation.surface: A bird that moves in lines or rows.
explanation.definitionFit: The crow-like bird shares its name with the chess piece moving straight along rows and columns.

clue.text: Not that Maeterlinck's bird was so sad

definitions.text: Not that Maeterlinck's bird was so sad

parts.words: Not that Maeterlinck's bird was so sad
parts.note: Maeterlinck wrote the play The ... Bird, a symbol of happiness, though the colour word also means downcast

explanation.surface: A remark that the playwright's famous bird was not actually unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Maeterlinck's play L'Oiseau bleu (The Blue Bird) has a bird of happiness, so it was hardly 'sad' despite its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of the bird in the play also means melancholy, though that bird stood for happiness.

clue.text: Addition to bill for Paul Revere for instance

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a parliamentary bill
Revere made a famous midnight horseback journey in 1775

explanation.surface: An extra clause in a law concerning an American patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode at midnight in 1775 to warn of the British advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An amending clause tacked onto legislation, and also a horseman such as Revere on his midnight ride.

clue.text: Stupid duck but a fantastic flier

parts.note: dumb means stupid
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so O

explanation.surface: A foolish duck that turns out to be an amazing flyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'duck' is a zero score in cricket, hence O. Disney's Dumbo is a flying elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's flying elephant uses his huge ears to soar, a fanciful aviator.

clue.text: Sort of thing one might do in a pool

definitions.text: thing one might do in a pool
definitions.meaning: what a typist does in an office typing pool, not a swimming pool

explanation.surface: Something you might do in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests swimming; a typing pool was an office of typists.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or category is a sort, and typists in an office pool tap out letters on keyboards.

clue.text: Poor journalist imprisoned by French marshal

indicators.note: the journalist is held inside the marshal's name, as in a cell

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A hard-up reporter is locked up by a Napoleonic soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The poor are in want, lacking money.

clue.text: Feast celebrated at end of World War I

definitions.text: Feast celebrated at end of World War I

parts.words: Feast celebrated at end of World War I
parts.note: the armistice was signed on 11 November 1918, the day of a saint's feast

explanation.surface: A celebration held when the First World War ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The Armistice of 11 November 1918 fell on St Martin's day, a traditional quarter-day feast.
explanation.definitionFit: St Martin's feast falls on 11 November, Armistice Day, which marked the close of the 1914-18 war.

clue.text: Great Macedonian pontiff or poet

parts.note: Alexander the Great was king of Macedon
the Pope is the Roman pontiff

explanation.surface: Choosing among a Macedonian conqueror, a pope or a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is just a link; Alexander Pope was an English 18th-century poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century author of The Rape of the Lock was an English verse writer.
